Variants.Content: The Lys family belonged to the powerful class of Myr. There are no permanent feudal seats in Myr, and wealthy influence comes from workshops, ship stocks, debts, and kin with access to governorship politics. Each generation of Lys has to choose between technical profits and political risks; over-squeezing craftsmen may make short-term profits, or the most valuable craftsmanship may be transferred to competitors. Myr is renowned for its fine craftsmanship and trade, with lenses, lace, carpets, dyes and Myr-style crossbows all requiring skilled craftsmen and imported raw materials. Cities were dominated by wealthy merchants, governors, and industrial interests, with wealth supported by slave labor and the skills of free artisans.
Entry Terys Exquisite goods are highly profitable, but a shortage of raw materials or a wrong move in diplomacy can shut down an entire workshop.
Entry Terys Nobles can sell lace thousands of miles away, but the person who really makes the needlework flawless is the person who hurts his eyes by the window.

Entry Terys Lys is a powerful family of Myr, and the family business must continue to operate in the midst of fine manufacturing, port trade, and competition among republican factions. The family crest is just a facade, the real weight of the family is whether they can protect their fiefdom, honor their engagements, and rally people in times of crisis.
